chunks: Hamzah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alavi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Bazzaz narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad Dawud ibn Suleiman al-Ghazi narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them) narrated to me, saying: My father Musa ibn Ja'far narrated to me, saying: My father Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated to me, saying: My father Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir narrated to me, saying: My father Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: My father al-Husayn ibn Ali narrated to me, saying: My father the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon them) narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Faith is affirmation by the tongue, knowledge by the heart, and action by the limbs.

Hamzah ibn Muhammad (may God be pleased with him) said: And I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatam saying: I heard my father saying: And this hadith has been narrated from Abu al-Salt al-Harawi Abd al-Salam ibn Salih, from Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them) with a similar chain of narrators. Abu Hatam said: 'If this chain of narrators were recited to a madman, he would be cured.'

key_terms.أَرْكَان: Limbs/Pillars (of the body used for worship)

ai.seo_question: What are the three components of faith according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the Shia doctrine of 'Iman bi-l-Qalb' (faith of the heart), emphasizing that internal conviction is the essential core, while verbal affirmation and physical action are its necessary manifestations. The chain of transmission highlights the continuous spiritual authority of the Ahl al-Bayt, reinforcing the Imams' role as authentic interpreters of faith. This tripartite definition distinguishes Shia theology from other schools by prioritizing the inner state of the believer as the foundation of religious identity.
